RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Jennings
Member ID: W530749089
Reference Number: POC-F7C299C469-49918
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-07-31
Requested Service/Procedure: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-27

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root, lumbar), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." I understand the applicable coverage policy to be Cigna's Medical Coverage Policy — Musculoskeletal: Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy), identified as CMM-606, developed by EviCore by Evernorth for Cigna, effective February 25, 2026 (Version 1.1.2025). If a different version or policy number was actually applied to this request, I ask that Cigna identify the exact policy and version relied upon and provide it to me, since the denial notice itself did not specify one.

The clinical record submitted with the original request demonstrates that Mr./Ms. Jennings meets the "Radiculopathy" indication criteria set out in CMM-606.2 of that policy for an initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy. The policy states:

"Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met..."

I address each associated criterion for the Radiculopathy pathway below, mapped to the clinical documentation in the prior authorization packet:

1. Subjective symptoms
Policy requirement: "Subjective symptoms include BOTH of the following: Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.) [and] Persistent radiating pain into the buttock(s) and/or lower extremity(ies)."

Clinical support: The patient has experienced 14 months of progressive lower back pain unrelieved by rest, cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and has radicular pain radiating into the right calf. This satisfies both the functional-impairment and persistent-radiating-pain components of this criterion.

2. Objective physical exam findings
Policy requirement: "Objective physical exam findings include EITHER of the following: Nerve root tension sign including ANY of the following: Positive straight leg raise, Crossed straight leg raise, Femoral stretch test [or] Neurologic deficit including ANY of the following: Dermatomal sensory deficit, Functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness), Reflex changes."

Clinical support: The exam notes document positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level (L4-L5/right L5 distribution). I ask that the reviewing physician confirm that the specific provocative test(s) and neurologic finding(s) documented in the enclosed exam note satisfy this criterion; if additional detail on the specific test or deficit is needed, we can supply an addendum from Dr. Okafor.

3. Trial and failure of conservative treatment
Policy requirement: "Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): Prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for six (6) weeks[;] Provider-directed exercise program prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician for six (6) weeks[;] Epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery."

Clinical support: The patient completed at least three qualifying, distinct conservative measures, all exceeding the six-week minimum specified: (a) NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; (b) a supervised physical therapy program (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility) over 12 weeks, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, with 16 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note; and (c) a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. [Please confirm whether the corticosteroid injection administered was an epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block performed at the L4-L5 level, as required by this criterion — this detail is not fully specified in the summary provided to me and I will supplement the record if needed.] Taken together, these records document less-than-meaningful, non-durable improvement with at least two, and arguably three, of the qualifying modalities.

4. Imaging confirmation
Policy requirement: "MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: Herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation)[,] Synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst[,] Central/lateral/foraminal stenosis[,] Osteophytes."

Clinical support: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-08 demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This finding is directly concordant with the patient's right-sided radicular pain into the calf and the corresponding neurologic exam findings, and it independently satisfies this criterion under both the "herniated disc(s)" and "lateral... stenosis" categories listed in the policy.

5. Absence of unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorder
Policy requirement: "Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)."

Clinical support: The record documents no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. No mental or behavioral health diagnosis is noted in the packet provided to me. [If Cigna's review identified a specific concern in this domain, please identify it so it can be addressed directly; otherwise this criterion appears to be met on the record as submitted.]

Based on the foregoing, the clinical documentation submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies each of the criteria set out in CMM-606.2 for the Radiculopathy indication for initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (CPT 63030). I therefore request that Cigna reverse the denial and approve the requested procedure.

In the event any single criterion above is found to be insufficiently documented, I request that Cigna specify precisely which criterion and sub-element it considers unmet, so that Dr. Okafor's office can submit a targeted addendum rather than have the appeal denied for lack of clarity.

Enclosed with this appeal are the following supporting records referenced above:
- Physical therapy discharge note (12-week course, 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, 16 visits)
- Medication/treatment history documenting 6 months of NSAID use and the 2026-04-20 corticosteroid injection and response
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-08
- Physical examination notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, MD [if available/attached]

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-27, and I am submitting it well in advance of that deadline. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise of the anticipated timeframe for a decision. If any portion of this appeal or the underlying denial was based on a policy document other than CMM-606 (Lumbar Microdiscectomy) as described above, please notify me immediately so that I may respond to the correct criteria.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

_____________________________
Taylor Jennings
Member ID: W530749089

cc: [Dr. Okafor, MD — Orthopedic Surgery]

Note to reader: Every passage above placed in quotation marks and attributed to the plan was taken verbatim from the retrieved text of Cigna/EviCore Medical Coverage Policy CMM-606, "Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy)," effective February 25, 2026 (V1.1.2025). All other statements are drawn from the clinical summary provided or are marked with bracketed placeholders where the record on hand does not contain the needed detail (e.g., the exact appeal mailing address/fax, the specific type of injection administered, and confirmation of the specific provocative test performed).
